The spec says "e-stop loop with multiple sink points (ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL) gated through single non-inverting buffers (SN74LVC1G07, parts U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks, feeding an ESTOP_OUT signal shared with the CAN connectors J2/J13."

Netlist:
U22: /OE = ESTOP_SINK1, A = GND, Y = U15.A
U15: /OE = ESTOP_SINK2, A = U22.Y, Y = U35.A
U35: /OE = ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL, A = U15.Y, Y = /ESTOP_SINK_ALL
U36: /OE = /ESTOP_SINK_ALL, A = ESTOP, Y = ESTOP_OUT

So the chain is: U22 is enabled when ESTOP_SINK1 is low. Its input is GND, so output low. U15 is enabled when ESTOP_SINK2 is low. Its input is U22.Y. If U22 is enabled, U22.Y is low, so U15 output low. If U22 is disabled, U22.Y is pulled high by R61, so U15 input high. U15 output follows input if enabled. U35 similarly. U36 is enabled when /ESTOP_SINK_ALL is low. Its input is ESTOP (from CM4). Its output is ESTOP_OUT.

So if any of ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL is low, the chain pulls /ESTOP_SINK_ALL low, which enables U36, so ESTOP_OUT follows ESTOP. If all sinks are high, /ESTOP_SINK_ALL is pulled high by R63, U36 is disabled, ESTOP_OUT is high-Z (pulled up by external?).

This is a wired-AND of the sink signals. The buffers are used as open-drain? Actually with 1G125, when enabled, they drive the output. If U22 is enabled, it drives low. If U15 is enabled and U22 is disabled, U15 input is high (pulled up), so U15 drives high. But U15 output is connected to U35 input. If U15 drives high, that's fine. But if U15 is disabled, its output is high-Z, pulled up by R62. So the chain works. However, if multiple buffers are enabled, could there be contention? U22 output is only connected to U15 input. U15 output only to U35 input. U35 output only to U36 /OE. So no contention. The only issue is if U15 is enabled and U22 is enabled, U22 drives low, U15 input low, U15 drives low. That's fine. If U15 is enabled and U22 is disabled, U22 output high-Z, pulled high by R61, U15 input high, U15 drives high. That's fine. So the circuit works with 1G125.
